stem: Which additional examination step should be included in the assessment of an infant with a possible acyanotic congenital heart lesion?

options.text: Palpation of the liver and spleen
Weber and Rinne tuning fork tests

explanation: Palpation of the liver and spleen is part of the structured examination for suspected congenital heart disease in an infant. It helps assess for hepatomegaly or splenomegaly as part of a broader cardiovascular review.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because palpation of the liver and spleen is explicitly included in the congenital heart disease examination work-up.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because formal visual field testing is a neurological or ophthalmic assessment, not part of this cardiac examination.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because Weber and Rinne tests assess hearing, not congenital heart disease.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because peak expiratory flow measures airway function and is not part of this cardiac work-up.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because ankle clonus is a neurological sign and is not included in the congenital heart disease assessment.
